_comment: Enemy numbers (task T-039): the minion, minion spawning, coin drops, the kaiju, its coins when defeated (task T-119) and its meteor attack. Distances in units (1 unit = the car's width), speeds in units per second, times in seconds, health in the same points as the weapons' damage (weapons.json); damage to the car in hearts (run.json car.starting_hearts). Knockback is a speed added to the car (the car's knockback function). Minion size_scale (T-379, board 2026-10-29): the minion is drawn this many times its old size (a whole number, so the pixel edges stay hard) and its body, hits and navigation radius grow to match; the kaiju is unchanged. Minion move_speed 4.2 is 30% below the old 6 (board, 2026-10-31, T-443). Enemies never get tougher over a run: only the number of minions grows (Enemies, Decisions). Proposed numbers; the board judges them in playtests. Reasons for each number: tasks/T-039-enemy-data.md, Result notes (kaiju_coins: tasks/T-119-kaiju-coins-data.md, Result notes).

death._comment: T-531 (Enemies, Decisions, 'Minion deaths', board 2026-11-03). corpse_seconds 2 and the fade after the last hit are the board's; every other number is a proposal for the playtest. animation_seconds 0.5: long enough to read a tip-over at 50 steps a second (25 frames) and short enough that a crowd's deaths do not pile up unseen; the PixelLab sheets (T-532) are played evenly over it. fade_seconds 0.4: a short fade so the body goes without a pop. max_corpses 24 whole corpses (the oldest fades at once when a 25th dies), at most 48 counting the fading ones (the oldest is freed at once): the weapons kill about 4 minions a second late in the run, so 2 s of corpses is about 8 and 24 is three times that, with room for a big bricks wave; max_droplets 80 and max_pools 160 are about 9 bursts of 9 and about 7 pools a corpse at most (droplets that land near a pool feed it instead of making a new one), so a mass death costs at most 24 spill nodes and about 300 small rectangles. Knock: slide_seconds 0.4 is the friction (a knock slides its distance and slows evenly to rest in 0.4 s, so it reads as a skid, not a teleport). Weapons push a corpse as far as they push a living minion (knock_scale_* 1.0: bricks 4 at tier 1, the wiper and the Polarized Steering Wheel's shock the same, from weapons.json), so a corpse flies as far as the minion would have. The car: the push is the car's speed in units a second times knock_car_per_speed 0.25 (cruise 11 gives 2.75 units, top speed about 20 gives 5), at least knock_car_min 1.5 and at most knock_car_max 8 (the car's own knockback on a living minion is 8), and only above knock_car_min_speed 2 so parking against a corpse does not keep it alive; the same corpse is pushed again at the earliest after knock_car_gap_seconds 0.2. Spill: droplets_per_death 9; droplet_speed 2.5 to 6 units a second along the ground and droplet_up 4 to 8 units a second up with droplet_gravity 24 units a second squared, so a droplet is in the air 0.33 to 0.67 s, rises 0.3 to 1.3 units and lands 1 to 4 units away (the minion is 1 unit across); pool_max_radius_px 7 screen pixels (a pool of three droplets is about as wide as the minion's body), pool_spread_seconds 0.35 (a pool grows from a speck to its size in that time), pool_max_seconds 8 (a corpse that is hit again and again keeps its pool no longer than this).

spawning._comment: T-443 (Enemies, Decisions, 'Minions spawn on a timer, and 30% slower', board 2026-10-31): minions spawn one after another on a timer, however many are already around, each spawn_margin_units beyond the edge of the visible screen (street only, clear of buildings and boulders). The spawn rate (minions per second, 1 / interval) grows in a straight line from 1 / spawn_interval_at_start_seconds at run second 0 to 1 / spawn_interval_at_boss_time_seconds at run second growth_until_seconds (T-522: the kaiju's arrival, now 3:00 in the 4-minute run; was 420 for the 7:00 arrival) and is then held; at the halfway mark (1:30) the interval is 1 / the average of the two rates (0.48 s). The combo's spawn multiplier (combo.json, spawning) multiplies the rate, so it divides the interval (x1.75 at its top: 0.3 s becomes about 0.17 s). max_minions_alive is a safety ceiling for the frame rate only: while that many are alive the timer waits. Proposals for the playtest (reasons: tasks/T-443-minions-spawn-on-timer.md, Result notes): 1.2 s at the start is about one per volley of the starting gun (base_fire_interval 1.2 s, one bullet kills a minion), so a player who shoots keeps up and one who does not sees a crowd build; 0.3 s at 7:00 is 4 a second, twice the old refill's top rate (one per 0.5 s), above what a mid-run gun alone kills, so the late run is crowded; about 870 minions over the old 7 minutes; T-522: the same two rates over 180 s, about 375 minions by 3:00. The ceiling 100 is five times the old top count (20), so it should not be met while the player drives and shoots (minions a whole screen behind are removed); it is there because the informal measurement (T-443's result notes) put the minions' physics step at about 0.2 ms per minion before T-444's optimisation, so 100 alive is about 20 ms a step, a whole frame. T-444 should raise it once the crowd is cheaper. The old wanted-count numbers (minions_at_start 12, minions_at_boss_time 20, spawn_interval_seconds 0.5) are gone.

health_drops._comment: Health pickups a killed minion drops (Enemies, Decisions, Health drops, 2026-10-21; T-220). drop_chance is rolled separately from the coins' (half the coins' rate by the board's decision, 2026-10-22, T-277: 0.3 against the coins' 0.6), restore_hearts is how many hearts one pickup restores (1), never above the maximum (T-333, hearts, 2026-10-28: drop_chance halved from 0.3 to 0.15, the heal from 30% of the health to 1 heart; T-371, 2026-10-29: drop_chance 1.5 times as often, 0.15 to 0.225). The kaiju drops none (a proposal for the playtest). Proposed numbers; the board judges them in playtests.

kaiju._comment: T-522 (Enemies, Decisions, 'Paced for the 4-minute run', board 2026-11-03): health 1500 (was 500 for the 8-minute run), a proposal for the playtest. Estimate: a 3-weapon build at 3:00 (gun at its last tier = old tier 8, 4 bullets x 4 damage at a 0.23 s interval, about 68 damage a second; the flame about 4 on the kaiju; a third weapon about 9) does about 81 a second if everything lands, so 1500 falls in about 19 s; the gun is shared with the crowd (closest enemy first), so at half that, about 40 a second, it takes about 37 s of the 60. A build whose gun is one tier short (about 21 a second) needs about 44 s if everything lands and does not finish in time at half effectiveness. The test in tests/unit/test_enemy_data.gd works it out from the weapon data.

kaiju_coins._comment: Coins the kaiju drops when defeated (Enemies, Decisions, 2026-10-13): always (drop_chance 1), coins_per_drop coins. Its death ends the run at once, so they are added to the run's coins as the run ends, without being picked up.

meteor_attack._comment: Attacks start first_attack_after_seconds after the kaiju appears, then every seconds_between_attacks. Each attack: windup_seconds of the kaiju's short animation, then meteors_per_attack warning circles at once, each landing warning_seconds later within land_within_units_of_car of the car. A meteor hits the car when the car's centre is within impact_radius_units of where it lands (the boulder's radius: boulders are 3 units across). warning_seconds is decided (Enemies, Decisions), not a balancing number. A boulder a meteor leaves stays boulder_lifetime_seconds after it lands (decided, Enemies, Decisions), then fades out over boulder_fade_seconds and is gone (T-142; the fade's length is a proposed number). A meteor's warning circle keeps boulder_clearance_units of free ground between its edge and any boulder a meteor left that still stands, fading or waiting included (T-147; a proposed number: the boulder's drawing is taller than its circle, so a circle touching it looked as if it was under it).
